title: How a Smoke Detector Works in 60 Seconds 🔥🚨 #shorts
description:
A smoke alarm hides a dark chamber that air drifts through. In photoelectric alarms, smoke scatters an LED beam onto a light sensor; in ionization alarms, smoke disrupts a tiny current made by a speck of americium. Either way, the chip sounds a horn of at least 85 decibels. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#smokedetector #firesafety #howitworks

steps.label: Hook
steps.text: A smoke alarm blasts at least *85 decibels*, loud enough to wake you up.

steps.label: Chamber
steps.text: Inside is a dark *chamber* with slots that let air and smoke drift in.

steps.label: Light
steps.text: In a photoelectric alarm, an *LED* shines across the chamber, aimed away from a *light sensor*.

steps.label: Scatter
steps.text: When smoke enters, its particles *scatter* the light onto the sensor.

steps.label: Ions
steps.text: Ionization alarms use a speck of *americium* to make a tiny current in the air. Smoke *disrupts* it.

steps.label: Alarm
steps.text: Either way, the chip sees the change and sounds the *horn*.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Smoke, signal, *siren*. Follow Inside 60 for more.
